extracted.intended_audience: reporters, editors, and newsroom staff interested in improving transparency in everyday journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations for reporters and newsrooms on daily practices to increase transparency: publishing primary sources and data, showing methods, teaching readers to verify, and making those practices routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily show-your-work practice
rubrics_metrics.description: "Here’s what we learned, here’s how we confirmed it, and here’s how you can do the same."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell readers every day what you learned, how you verified it, and how readers can replicate or confirm the reporting. The author positions this as a daily routine rather than occasional transparency gestures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish primary documents and data alongside stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish primary records, court documents, and the evidence that underpins reporting online with your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: uploading and embedding records using services like DocumentCloud; "posted all the evidence along with my story, inviting readers to make up their own minds." Anti-pattern: withholding primary documents or summarizing without links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to references in your stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Include links to references and sources directly in articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes many newsrooms still fail to do the basics: link to references in your stories. This is presented as a low-effort/high-value step toward transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tools to make sharing quick and easy
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt and evangelize tools (e.g., DocumentCloud) to upload, organize, and embed records and excerpts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: use DocumentCloud to upload and organize countless records and embed pages/excerpts in stories. The emphasis is on choosing tools that lower the friction of sharing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite interrogation of your data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide readers with access and interfaces to probe and interrogate the datasets underlying reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage skepticism by giving readers the means to examine the data themselves (interactive sidebars, datasets, databases). The author argues newsrooms should "invite interrogations into your data."

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach readers how to interpret and obtain primary records
rubrics_metrics.description: Go beyond publishing documents: explain how readers can interpret them and how to obtain similar primary records themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article suggests newsrooms should "teach them how to interpret and interrogate them, how to obtain primary records themselves," treating transparency also as public education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with data reporters to convert records into analyzable datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with data journalists to transform paper records into structured databases for novel reporting and public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: turning hundreds of pages of paper records into a first-of-its-kind state database of deaths in police custody. Collaboration expands what can be shown and verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make data-quality issues a reporting focus
rubrics_metrics.description: When evidence or data collected by authorities is weak or flawed, report on that weakness as an important story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a reporter finding state bias crime data was garbage and making the weakness of the evidence the subject of the story itself. Transparency includes exposing bad data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate reporting process and "shoe leather"
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the effort, methods, and steps you took to produce a story (the 'shoe leather').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author urges journalists to "do everything in your power to demonstrate the shoe leather that went into 650 words of copy," i.e., explain methods, source contact, verification steps rather than just publishing conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalize sharing primary sources as routine practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the sharing of primary sources and transparency practices regular, embedded parts of newsroom routines rather than ad-hoc actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece criticizes that "hardly anybody is making the sharing of primary sources a regular part of their daily journalism," calling for newsrooms to 'bake such transparency into our routines.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Build trust by welcoming scrutiny rather than lamenting skepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to public distrust by exposing evidence and verification steps; encourage reader skepticism as a check rather than resisting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues newsrooms should "encourage" skepticism and show their work to regain trust, rather than merely bemoaning public distrust or attacking skeptics.
